title: Mirror and Lantern
subtitle: You and I met, and the room was aglow with light.

content.text: The Danube, a river born from dewdrops grown into a mighty course. She is a mother to many children, and all are eager to be fed.
Here is the empire founded by two of her strongest children—a rich and admirable duo.
There is an alluring charm to the music of Musikverein, captivating everyone who visits this place. I can talk about its art all day, and that's just the beginning!
There are 11 children in this empire. When bond together, they are invincible.
See, the flourishing cities, the cheering citizens, even the chirping birds are singing a song of a land of freedom.

branch.text: Heh heh ho. You're familiar with the devils in the detail.
Ah. You're just buying everything I'm selling. Be smart, my dear.
You'll see, if we dive deeper, you'll see something different.
You'll see charity dances raising funds for the poor. The icing on the cake for the philanthropist, they said, though no one knows where the money goes.
You'll see mice eating the bodies of the beggars, the arcanists being ousted from their arts, and poverty spreading its misery like an illness.
Except in the great duo, Austria and Hungary, in the vast and intimidating centers of power they've built together.
The other children, however, were shut out at the door. They may have their talents, but that alone cannot buy them a place at the table.
Bohemia, Moravia ... The empire has only the slightest sympathy to these forgotten children, nothing more than articles of fine words written in the newspapers.
How funny it is. To see these poor humans now sharing in the same fate as the arcanists.
Do you think they will choose to hold together, even if left outside of the negotiation table?

content.text: Cooperation is the only way they can survive.

branch.text: That's no small task. A chain is only as strong as its weakest link. An age-old story.
Oh. So you're a pessimist. Then, I guess, you will enjoy the drama of this broken family.
The truth is, they will fight each other like rats in the barrel, until every one of them falls.
Crack, crack. Did you hear it? It's the fracturing of a great empire, like the breaking of spring ice.
In an army that speaks twenty different languages, who can a general trust to obey his commands?
Only those who speak the language he does.
You can already imagine it—a ridiculous beast with 11 limbs, each pulling in their own direction, limping across the battlefield until it gets shot ...
Luckily, that time hasn't come yet.
The crying of the children is still being drowned out by the music playing in the theater, and the beating hearts within the dancers' chests.
The wails of suffering are silent in the newspapers, and the world sees only the silvery mirage of freedom and prosperity.
Believing all these children can live in harmony.
But my darling, we know that the ice must break. It's as inevitable as the thaw of spring.

items.text: Mirror and Lantern

items.speaker: Vendor I
items.text: Kakania! This way! Over here!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Illich! Thanks a lot! The prop sure came in handy.
Kakania tears off her fake beard, fanning herself with her hand.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Mmm ... Ugh! Phew, finally. Why do I keep having things stick to my lips ...

items.speaker: Vendor I
items.text: Hah! Be careful with that. It is no ordinary beard! Every single strand was soaked in a Bohemian potion mixed with bloodroot, toad's heart, and javangall ...

items.speaker: Vendor I
items.text: Why were the guards after you?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: That's a long story.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: And oh, don't worry about this kind little lady. She saved my life, and she's a half ... a third of a friend!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: A third of ...
She discreetly releases the button of the communicator in her pocket.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Ugh ... This is bad, the connection is down, I can't get in touch with Madam Hofmann.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: She's probably in an important conversation with the Field Agent Squad and has calls on block ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: It's okay, Marcus, you can do this yourself, just stay in the conversation! Communication is not that hard. You've done this through before. You can do it!
Despite having written about a thousand ways to start a conversation, she never expected to find herself in a situation like this.
Marcus frantically racks her mind for topics to discuss. Fortunately, everyone present is far more talkative than she is.

items.speaker: Vendor I
items.text: My, my, Kakania! Are you friends with government officials now?

items.speaker: Vendor I
items.text: Times have changed indeed! I've been here for a whole year, but I've never seen an official without a beard!

items.speaker: Vendor I
items.text: Where are you from? Croatia? Moravia? Galicia?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I grew up in Romania ...

items.speaker: Vendor I
items.text: Oh, I'm from Bosnia and Herzegovina ... That makes us friends, since we're both from somewhere-nia! Gahaha!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Be careful on the streets these days, Illich. You could be in trouble too if the guards catch you! After all, you haven't got a license.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Eh? You don't?

items.speaker: Vendor I
items.text: Oh, of course not! Have you read the requirements? "Records of the safe use of arcane skills within three generations" ... I was born in the streets, I don't even know who my grandmother was.

items.speaker: Vendor I
items.text: And the records aren't the hard part to get around. If you're applying in Vienna, the license has to be issued by the central government.

items.speaker: Vendor I
items.text: It's not an Austrian problem, nor a Hungarian problem. The central government sits in the middle ...

items.speaker: Vendor I
items.text: ... and no official has any idea of what's what—should this be the Kaiser's concern? Or the König's? Or both?

items.speaker: Vendor I
items.text: You'd be the biggest fool to listen and follow these broken rules! Stuck in the system, nowhere to go ... unless you work the magic of krones ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: ... What happens if we don't have an arcanum license?

items.speaker: Vendor I
items.text: Oh, you'll love this.

items.speaker: Vendor I
items.text: Who knows. You could get 3 days in detention, or maybe 10 years in prison. Even if you are sentenced to prison, they might forget to bring you in.

items.speaker: Vendor I
items.text: Or, if you're an outstanding citizen who can shed your arcanum during your human re-education, you might get to have a nice life—without a license that is.

items.speaker: Vendor I
items.text: Our justice system is much more unpredictable than the arcanists'. We still have a fair chance of getting away!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Very informative, Illich.
Kakania clears her throat, still somewhat guarded, and flashes out a meaningful glance.

items.speaker: Vendor I
items.text: Oh, well then ... See you, Kakania and Ms. Foundation. Forget I said anything!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: They are ...?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Some arcanist kids on the streets. I'm surprised you know nothing about them. The country has changed, lady, and not everything in Vienna is as decent and sumptuous as the buildings on the Ring Road and Herrengasse.
Her tone belies a hint of sarcasm.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I'm thankful for your help, Ms. Foundation, but so far I have returned the favor—you don't want the guards either, do you? We're even.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: So can you tell me why you're here?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Oh, I see. Mr. Karl sent you, didn't he? Because I don't have a psychiatrist's license. Can't you people give me a break?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I swear on my ancestors, I'm doing this entirely the arcanist way. It has nothing to do with human science!
She poses a question but leaves no room for an answer. Leaning closer to Marcus, she pushes her glasses up with suspicion.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Don't you people ever sleep? Do you not have a life? This is the tenth time this month, even God rests after working six days in a row!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I have an arcanum license inherited from my family, it's nothing to be ashamed of. My fees are reasonable, no one's ever complained ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: No, um, Ms. Kakania, this is really coincidental ... I ... Err ... I just happened to know that you are a psychiatrist ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Hm? So? Are psychiatrists considered doctors now?
Maintaining her barriers of politeness against the rapid topic changes feels like holding a smile in a hailstorm.
On the verge of tears, Marcus desperately falls back to the Field Mission Manual.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I think there's been a misunderstanding. We-I'm not here to check your credentials.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Then what?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: So, you call yourself Kakania, but I know your first name is Klara ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Oh, I didn't know the Foundation staff reads my work. How very flattering!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Yes, I'm Klara. But Ms. Foundation, don't you think Kakania is an intriguing name? Heinrich—who is a friend of mine—gave me a book which greatly inspired me.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Our country is just like that name. It both is, and isn't; it both has, and has not. If you look for it, it can't be found. Yet if you stop looking, it's everywhere.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Look at this country, my friend!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: The sumptuous buildings rise so high ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: that the people in power never have to lay eyes on the rye farmers of Bohemia, the immigrants from the east coast of Adriatic Sea, or on the arcanists!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: How could there possibly be smog choking the industrial area? How could there possibly be cold houses in the winter? The coffee house is definitely filled with people who love to dance, and not with those who can't afford the heat, oh no.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Surely there's no bureaucracy, no discrimination, no poverty here. This is a city of humanism and freedom, oh yes.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Kakania ... "kaiserlich-königlich," or "kaiserlich und königlich," and ... "Caca-nia," the s**tland! Hahaha, there's no better name for this country.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: So then, you did get that book, from a friend ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Now's my chance. I still have one "Spider Tail" Madam Hofmann left me.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: If I can find a chance to leave the Spider Tail on her ... Or in her place ...
The young assistant takes a deep breath.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I ... I'm intrigued by the book. Can I see it?
Cemetery
This concludes the report by Semmelweis of the Field Agent Administration. Please confirm, Madam Hofmann.
In the corner, Hofmann holds her communicator out with brow furrowed.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Yes, report received.
Haha, why so serious, Greta? That was just routine.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: And I envy your lightheartedness and optimism. They got you out of Vienna on such short notice, I can only imagine that it must have been difficult for you as well.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: According to your intel, the Empire's had too many assassinations in a short period of time. This is not good for the Critical Point, Semmelweis.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: At least try to stay in a good mood. What else can we do?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Aside from that, Greta, I have more to tell you. I was pulled out of Vienna overnight and I didn't have time to brief the new squad there.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: You know, it takes ages to get through the briefing process. I might as well just tell you now, personally.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: There could be an arcanist who has crossed the "Storm," and is now in Vienna.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: What did you say? Do we know more about this arcanist?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: We only know his name is Heinrich. We learned about this from the Berlin squad when we met up here, but had no time to verify.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: I see. Leave the rest to us.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: If true, he traveled to Berlin during the sixth "Storm" and survived the 1913 "Storm" there. And after the 1966 "Storm," and the one in 1929 ...

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: And now it's 1913 for the second time. For all the arcanists who crossed the sixth "Storm," this is exciting news.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Mmhmm. Their time has returned.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: I understand the excitement, but perhaps time, in its chaotic fashion, has inadvertently returned to the same year.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: I hear you, Semmelweis. This is valuable information, I'll let the ...

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Greta? Are you still there?

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Sorry, I have to go ...

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Something's wrong with the "Spider Tail" I left on Marcus. This is not her ritual ... Something's happened.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I'm surprised, Ms. Marcus, you know so much about this era!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I thought the Foundation was nothing but bureaucrats and bookworms. Oh, have you been to the Secession Building? Did you like it? Shame that book isn't there.
Kakania finally finds the key.
Clinic

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Please, come in! Forgive the mess. I must say that it is at least more orderly than the administration of the Empire.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Than-thank you.
The room resembles a studio more so than a clinic.
The scene is scattered about with unfinished paintings, dried paints, stage props, and posters.
And mirrors. Many, many mirrors.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: These are stage props, Heinrich left them here. He certainly learned some useful things in Berlin.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Make yourself comfortable. I'll get you some tea, and look for the book.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Please don't bother, Ms. Kakania! I won't stay long, I have to go back to the branch soon.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I just need to confirm that you have that book with you ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Ooh!
The clinic's curtains are tightly drawn, blocking out the day, yet her mirrors flash with light for a second.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Is this ... Kakania's arcane skill?
Marcus quickly covers her eyes with her hands, stepping back toward the door.
Kakania's cheerful voice rings from the other side.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Ms. Foundation, it's okay! Just a little trick I use to ensure my personal safety. I usually even charge for this!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: "Look into the mirror, which reflects your inner world" ... This trick has been used by arcanists for thousands of years. When it was first used, the Roman Emperors still ruled this land.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Speaking of which, Ms. Foundation ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: How did you know that the pistol was tampered with? Your arcane skill?
Though it might only be some sort of trick of psychology—the mirror's glare becomes increasingly blinding.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: ... Um, don't look at the mirror!
The investigator braces herself as she grips the lamp, ready for combat at a moment's notice.
Kakania's tone remains gentle, as if soothing one of her patients.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I am curious. No need to be alarmed—I'll treat you gently.
TO BE CONTINUED…
